# `js/prefer-temporal-conversion`

**A `Temporal` conversion method instead of rebuilding the value**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does (the conversion is exact for a direct `from(source)`, a nanosecond-based `Instant`, a serialization into a plain type and a complete time-field rebuild, and is made; millisecond-based `Instant`s lose submillisecond precision, serialization into an `Instant` can lose seconds, and a date-bearing property bag without a calendar defaults to ISO 8601, so those are suggestions; a comment inside leaves the report without a fix) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/prefer-temporal-conversion` |

## What it checks

`Temporal.Instant.from(zoned)`, `Temporal.Instant.fromEpochNanoseconds(zoned.epochNanoseconds)`, `Temporal.PlainDate.from(zoned.toString())`, `new Temporal.PlainDate(zoned.year, zoned.month, zoned.day)` and the property-bag forms are reported when the source is known to be a `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` (to `Instant`, `PlainDateTime`, `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`) or a `Temporal.PlainDateTime` (to `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`): use `zoned.toInstant()`, `.toPlainDateTime()`, `.toPlainDate()`, `.toPlainTime()`. A source is known by `new Temporal.X()`, `Temporal.X.from()`, `Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO()`/`plainDateTimeISO()`, an annotation `Temporal.X`, or a `const` alias of one. Rebuilds that copy only some fields, add or change one, mix receivers or take options are not reported.

**Why:** The conversion method keeps every field, including the sub-millisecond ones and the calendar, that a rebuild by hand can drop.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/prefer-temporal-conversion" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/prefer-temporal-conversion" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/prefer-temporal-conversion" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/prefer-temporal-conversion" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/prefer-temporal-conversion" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/prefer-temporal-conversion": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/prefer-temporal-conversion: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/prefer-temporal-conversion expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/prefer-temporal-conversion --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/prefer-temporal-conversion       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/prefer-temporal-conversion  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                 # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
const zoned = Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO();
const day = Temporal.PlainDate.from(zoned);
```

#### Do

```js
const zoned = Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO();
const day = zoned.toPlainDate();
```

#### Fixed

```js
const zoned = Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO();
const day = zoned.toPlainDate();
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
const zoned = Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO();
const day = Temporal.PlainDate.from(zoned);
```

#### Do
